draft.title: Subverting text conventions
card: A convention is a usual feature of a genre or text type. Readers expect it. For example, a fairy tale often begins with "Once upon a time" and ends with a happy ending.
To subvert a convention is to break or twist it on purpose. An author might start a story at its end, or give a hero a sad ending.
Subverting works because readers notice what they expected and did not get. This can surprise them or make them think.
Authors subvert conventions to make a point. A fairy tale where the villain tells the story may make readers question whose side they usually hear.
draft.remember: Breaking a genre's usual pattern on purpose can surprise readers and make them think.

a.q: A detective story names the criminal on page one, then spends the book on why the crime happened. How does this subvert the genre?
opts: It breaks the usual pattern of keeping the culprit hidden
It follows the usual pattern of a mystery with a hidden culprit
It repeats the same pattern used in a fairy tale
It turns the story into a genre with no conventions
a.why: Readers of detective stories usually expect the culprit to stay hidden until the end. Naming the culprit early breaks that expectation on purpose. It does not follow the pattern, so the option saying it does is wrong.
a.clue: What do readers of this genre usually expect about the culprit?

b.q: Ravi writes a fairy tale in which the princess leaves the castle to start a bakery, and no prince appears. What is the most likely reason for this choice?
opts: To challenge the usual idea that a princess needs rescuing
To make the story fit the usual fairy tale pattern
To show that Ravi did not know the genre's conventions
To make the story a news report instead of a fairy tale
b.why: Fairy tales often have a princess who is rescued or marries a prince. Ravi twists this on purpose, which can make readers question that idea. Following the pattern would not be subverting it, so that option is wrong.
b.clue: Think about what a fairy tale princess usually does.
